html:
The Cheraw, also called the Saura or Saraw, were a Siouan-speaking people of the Piedmont of North Carolina, near the Sauratown Mountains and the Dan River. The map also shows them under their other name, Saura.

Spanish expeditions of the 1500s, starting with Hernando de Soto's in 1540, probably passed through their land. By the late 1600s raids by the Haudenosaunee and slave raids tied to the Carolina trade pushed them south to the Pee Dee River, on the border of the two Carolinas.

They fought the English colonists in the Yamasee War of 1715. Afterwards, weakened by war and disease, most joined the Catawba in the 1730s. The town of Cheraw, South Carolina, keeps their name.
